contradictions.title: CC-04 naming collision across evidence generations
contradictions.description: F0-004 (and F2-PREP-003/004, which cite it) use 'CC-04' to mean the Appointment booking/cancellation command contract. F2-PREP-002 independently defines its own 'F2-CC-04' as ContactRequestCommand.upsert() — a different, unrelated candidate. The bare string 'CC-04' does not appear anywhere in F2-PREP-002's two files.
contradictions.resolution: This charter uses 'CC-04' exclusively in the F0-004/ADR-015/F2-PREP-003/004 sense (Appointment booking/cancellation command). F2-PREP-002's 'F2-CC-04' is a distinct candidate and should be renumbered (e.g. to a non-colliding prefix) in any future consolidated contract catalog to prevent confusion. No sibling evidence file was edited to fix this — it is a naming-scheme collision between independently authored documents, not a factual error in either.
contradictions.severity: Low (documentation clarity only, no evidentiary conflict)

contradictions.title: F2-PREP-001's own ownership-ambiguity summary table disagrees with its own per-domain free-text field for 4 domains

F2-PREP-001 is not edited — this is a table-vs-field-text nuance, not a proven factual error requiring correction of historical evidence.

contradictions.title: F2-PREP-004 uses an informal 10-domain grouping, not the accepted 38-domain F2-PREP-001 taxonomy
contradictions.description: F2-PREP-004's original scoring pass (barred from reading F2-PREP-001 at the time) scored candidates named 'Imaging', 'Billing', 'Patients', 'Messaging', 'AI', etc. as informal groupings, not by F2-PREP-001's canonical domain codes. Its R1/R2 reconciliation passes confirmed no score changed against the merged inventory but did not remap its candidates onto exact domain codes.
contradictions.resolution: This charter performs that remapping explicitly: F2-PREP-004 'Imaging' = {IMG, BRG}; 'Billing' = {TRC, PAY, FIN} (approximately, per its own installment/payout/earnings-focused rationale — INS is not part of F2-PREP-004's 'Billing'); 'Messaging' = {WHA, IGM, SMS, EML}; 'AI' = {AIO, PAI}; 'Patients' = {PAT}; 'Privacy/retention/consent' = {PRV}; 'Appointments' = {APT}; 'Inventory' = {INV}; 'Notifications' = {NTF}; 'Integrations' = ambiguous/pre-EXC, likely a proxy for adapter-shaped domains generally (not a clean 1:1 match to any single F2-PREP-001 code).
contradictions.severity: Medium (necessary for the candidate matrix in this charter to cite F2-PREP-001 domain codes accurately)

contradictions.title: Billing's pilot favorability is materially contradicted between F2-PREP-004 and F2-PREP-002
contradictions.description: F2-PREP-004 scored Billing's boundary clarity and current coupling at 5/5 ('equal-lowest coupling by import analysis'), based on an import-level fan-in/fan-out pass. F2-PREP-002's later, deeper route-to-Prisma-model audit of the same functional area (BIL slice, 18 edges + 5 direct-Prisma-access sites) found 8 CROSS_DOMAIN_VIOLATION edges, 3 Critical-priority non-atomic financial-write sites, and the audit's single largest ownership-ambiguity finding (BIL-17).
contradictions.resolution: This is the most significant reconciliation in this charter. Billing's fallback-candidate status is preserved but downgraded from unconditional to conditional: it is NOT a clean fallback until BIL-17 (Service/AppointmentType dual identity) is resolved and BIL-08/BIL-09/BIL-10 (non-atomic installment/payout writes) are remediated. F2-PREP-004's favorable score is not treated as wrong — it measured a different, shallower signal (import-level coupling) — but it is superseded for pilot-selection purposes by F2-PREP-002's deeper evidence where the two conflict.
contradictions.severity: High (directly affects the pilot decision and fallback-candidate framing)

contradictions.title: External Calendar Integration was never scored by F2-PREP-004

externalCalendarIntegration.source: Not scored by F2-PREP-004 (contradiction C6). Derived by this charter (F2P5) from F2-PREP-001 EXC domain profile and F2-PREP-002 INF-01..08 / APT-11 / APT-23 edges. Lower confidence than Imaging/Billing scores.
externalCalendarIntegration.confidenceLevel: MEDIUM-LOW — first-pass derivation, not independently researched at F2-PREP-004's depth

evidenceNotes.boundaryClarity: F2P1: 'of all 38 domains in this inventory, External Calendar Integration is the only one that already exhibits essentially the full target module shape' — but F2P1 also flags this as a factual observation, not a selection, and its dependency edges are 'not yet independently verified against the accepted F0-004 833-edge matrix.' evidenceNotes.currentCoupling: F2P2 INF-01/02/03/05/06 + APT-11/23 are SAME_DOMAIN_ALLOWED or PUBLIC_CONTRACT_CANDIDATE; only INF-04 (calling Messaging's appointmentRequestNotification.ts) is a soft CROSS_DOMAIN_VIOLATION, Medium risk. Net: ~7-8 touched edges, 1 soft violation — comparable to or better than Imaging.
evidenceNotes.tenantKvkkSecurityRisk: F2P1 rates EXC securitySensitivity HIGH specifically due to encrypted OAuth2 client-secret + webhook-HMAC credential handling — a materially different (higher) security-sensitivity profile than Imaging or Billing, even though tenant isolation itself is clean (ExternalCalendarIntegration.clinicId is @unique).
evidenceNotes.dataOwnershipClarity: EXC's own models (ExternalCalendarIntegration/Mapping/InboundEvent/AppointmentLink) are clearly EXC-owned. ExternalCalendarAppointmentLink.appointmentId is a direct FK into Appointment 'with no contract' — a formalization gap, not an ownership ambiguity per se.
evidenceNotes.migrationComplexity: F2P1/F2P4 both describe EXC as 'clean-slate' — 'no legacy code to migrate, already provider-port-shaped' (F2P4 §3, quoting F2P1's own finding).
evidenceNotes.testCoverage: NO EVIDENCE. Neither F2-PREP-001, F2-PREP-002, nor F2-PREP-004 gives an EXC-specific test-coverage figure. Marked null (insufficient evidence) rather than invented — this is itself a blocker for any future pilot-readiness claim about EXC.
evidenceNotes.independentChangeCadence: SCORED UNFAVORABLY. `git log --grep=external.calendar -i --since=2026-07-20` shows PRs #266, #271, #273, #275 (outbound-sync phase 2, DigiDentiS v3.2.0 reconciliation, HMAC auth hardening) all landed in the days immediately preceding this task's baseline — the domain is under unusually active concurrent development, raising execution risk for freezing a pilot contract right now.
evidenceNotes.externalProtocolAdaptorPressure: Highest of the three candidates by design — EXC's entire reason for being is the DigiDentiS external protocol adapter, already built with a provider-factory pattern (ExternalCalendarProvider.ts + externalCalendarProviderFactory.ts) intended for future providers.
evidenceNotes.clickUpBusinessDemand: F2P3: 0 of 17 backlog items touch calendar-sync functionality ('None of the 17 items touch calendar-sync functionality, so EXC was not forced onto any item merely because the domain now exists').
evidenceNotes.abilityToDemonstrateBoundaryWithoutDistr: Scored highest of the three: EXC already demonstrates a real external-HTTP/webhook/OAuth adapter boundary entirely in-process, without any new deployment unit — arguably the clearest existing proof that the program's 'no new deployment unit without a measurable trigger' constraint is achievable in practice.

The Windows bridge agent already runs as a genuinely separate process on clinic-local hardware, communicating only via the existing public HTTP API — this is a pre-existing, accepted architecture, not a new deployment-boundary decision made by this charter.

forbiddenDirectAccess.principle: No direct cross-domain private access may be accepted as the desired target anywhere in the program. Cross-domain interaction must move toward accepted public contracts (additive, expand-migrate-contract).
forbiddenDirectAccess.top20RemediationCarriedForward: F2-PREP-002's ranked top-20 remediation list (8 Critical, 7 High, 5 Medium) is carried forward as unresolved program backlog by this charter, not resolved. The Critical tier (installment payoff, payout create/delete, patient anonymization non-atomicity, retention-sweep coupling, legacy WhatsApp tenant-resolution defect, WhatsApp/Instagram booking-concurrency race x2) requires separate authorization to remediate — none of it is authorized by this charter.

toolingDecision.scope: Report-only, non-blocking, scoped initially to the Imaging pilot boundary only once its contract is formally defined (per F2-PREP-004's own M0 recommendation). This is explicitly a POC, not production enforcement.
rationale: dependency-cruiser is the only tool evaluated in any depth by any F2-PREP task (F2-PREP-004 §5) — F2-PREP-001/002/003 do not mention boundary-enforcement tooling at all.

No functional ESLint setup currently exists in this repository (confirmed: no eslint.config.js anywhere), ruling out eslint-plugin-boundaries as an immediate option without first fixing that separately-scoped gap.
CodeGraph-based enforcement is confirmed unavailable in this environment (at least 7 independent prior tasks, per F2-PREP-002's own methodology note).
TypeScript path aliases alone cannot actually forbid an import — insufficient as an enforcement mechanism on their own.
madge is recommended by F2-PREP-004 only as a companion diagnostic, not primary enforcement (lacks a first-class forbidden-edge/contract concept).
A custom static import checker was explicitly not recommended first by F2-PREP-004 due to higher authorship/maintenance cost relative to an existing tool.
toolingDecision.explicitCaveat: This decision approves a bounded POC only. It does not commit the program to dependency-cruiser as final enforcement tooling, does not authorize CI-blocking mode, and does not apply to any domain other than the selected pilot's boundary.

toolingAcceptanceCriteria: TypeScript/ESM compatibility: must run cleanly against the existing server/ TypeScript + Node ESM setup with zero source changes required for the POC itself.

Monorepo/path compatibility: N/A in the strict sense (root + server/ are two npm projects, no npm workspaces) — must be verified to work correctly across that split without requiring workspace tooling to be introduced.
False-positive rate: must be near-zero against the Imaging pilot's already-documented clean boundary (F2P2 IMG-01..15) before being trusted for any other domain.

Support for allowed public contracts: must be able to express an explicit allowlist for the accepted transitional exceptions (e.g. Privacy's IMG-15 lifecycle-field access) without those being flagged as violations.
CI execution time: must add no more than a small, bounded amount of time to the existing Layer 1 static-check job (ci-layers.yml) — must not become a new slow layer.
Deterministic output: identical input must produce identical pass/fail output across runs (no flaky boundary findings).
Maintainability: config must be reviewable by someone without deep dependency-cruiser expertise (plain JSON/JS rule config, not a bespoke DSL requiring specialized knowledge).
Incremental adoption: must support scoping rules to only the pilot boundary initially, with a clear path to widen scope domain-by-domain later — never a repository-wide big-bang rule set.

Ability to enforce only new/changed code initially: report-only mode first; any future move to blocking mode must be a separate, explicitly approved decision, and even then should be evaluated for a warn-on-existing/block-on-new adoption path.

Rollback/removal path: must be removable by deleting its config file and CI step with zero impact on application runtime behavior (it is a dev-time static-analysis tool only, never a runtime dependency).

sequencing.note: Every step below requires separate approval before execution. Nothing in this charter authorizes moving past step 1.

steps.name: External review and approval of this charter
Pilot contract task: formalize Imaging's public contract (routes, commands, queries, events) per publicContractSummary above, no code change
Characterization tests: close Imaging's test-coverage gap for currently-unverified live-file-storage/live-DB paths (F2P4 §3 point 6) before any refactor
dependency-cruiser POC: report-only, scoped to Imaging boundary, per toolingDecision
Additive facade/public API: introduce named port/contract functions alongside existing direct-call paths (no removal yet)
Caller migration: move each known caller (Patients read, Privacy lifecycle exception, Notifications digest) onto the new contract one at a time
Enforcement in warning mode: dependency-cruiser (if POC accepted) flags any new direct-access attempt without failing CI
Enforcement in blocking mode: only after warning-mode POC demonstrates near-zero false positives over a meaningful period
